sentences.en: And the loot that gets sent back to Syria is so overwhelming that Spain comes to seem to the eyes of the

sentences.en: Yomaids back in Syria, a kind of land of wonders.

sentences.en: It's a place of talking statues where cities are fashioned entirely out of brass, just full of treasure and also full of slaves.

sentences.en: They all fall.
sentences.zh: 从本质上讲，除了西班牙北部的一些边缘地区之外，

sentences.en: have fallen in the space of basically a decade to these invaders.

sentences.zh: 并且基本上对曾经属于罗马高卢领土的

sentences.zh: 它就蕴含在这份成功本身之中。

sentences.en: So yes, as you say, Clothar II had patched together all the various parts of what had been Roman Gaul.

sentences.en: But the reason why this ultimately is not good for the Merovingian dynasty is that basically it's too large, it turns out, for Clothar II and his son and heir, Dagobert, to rule.
sentences.zh: 但这对墨洛温王朝来说最终并非好事，原因在于事实证明，对于克洛塔尔二世以及他的儿子兼继承人达戈贝尔特来说，这个版图实在是太大了，根本无法统治。

sentences.en: So what Clothar ends up having to do is to essentially send his sons out to rule as kind of sub-kings.

sentences.en: Dagobert, Clothar's son, he's sent off to rule Austrasia.
sentences.zh: 克洛塔尔的儿子达戈贝尔特被派去统治奥斯特拉西亚。

sentences.en: He's slightly more efficient.

sentences.zh: 但当他抵达时，他还年轻，缺乏经验。

sentences.en: And these are the guys who had got together to overthrow Brunhild.
sentences.zh: 正是这些人联合起来推翻了布伦希尔德。

sentences.en: They'd betrayed her.
sentences.zh: 他们背叛了她。

sentences.en: And so she'd ended up being captured by Clothar and very horribly executed.
sentences.zh: 所以她最终被克洛塔尔俘虏，并受到了极其残酷的处决。

sentences.en: So Arnulf serves the young Dagobert as his kind of preeminent counsellor.

sentences.zh: 他在拉丁语中的身份是宫相，也就是你可以把它英语化为“Major domo”。

sentences.en: His mayor, he's the leading official.
sentences.zh: 他是宫相，是首席官员。

sentences.en: And these officials are very, very ambitious.

sentences.en: And I guess traditionally, so going back to the time of Clovis, the role of these mayores, these mayors, let's call them that, was to kind of mediate between the king and
sentences.zh: 我想传统上，也就是追溯到克洛维时代，这些宫相（咱们就这么叫他们）的角色是在国王和

sentences.en: the local magnates, the local lords.

sentences.en: And this couple, they have a son who is absolutely kind of in every sense, a chip off the old block.
sentences.zh: 这对夫妇生了一个儿子，在各个意义上都绝对是其父（或祖）之风。

sentences.en: So he, like his grandfather, is also called Pepin.
sentences.zh: 所以他像他的祖父一样，也叫丕平。

sentences.en: So he's called Pepin of Hairstyle by the chroniclers to distinguish him from his grandfather.
sentences.zh: 为了把他和祖父区分开来，编年史家称他为主持丕平。

sentences.zh: 他在680年成为了奥斯特拉西亚的宫相。

sentences.en: And I mean, he's not just the power behind the throne.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他不仅仅是王位背后的权臣。

sentences.en: He puts the throne in his shadow.
sentences.zh: 他把王位笼罩在自己的阴影之下。

sentences.en: He is an absolutely domineering figure.

sentences.en: the mayor, but also of Neustria, that northern kingdom of Burgundy.
sentences.zh: ，还成为了北方王国纽斯特里亚和勃艮第的主人。

sentences.zh: 法兰克人的公爵兼亲王（Dux et Princeps Francorum）。

sentences.zh: 并且他把这个头衔确立为世袭的，就好像它是一种王权一样。

sentences.zh: 因此毫无意外地，

sentences.en: One went before the sun, rising in the morning.
sentences.zh: 一颗在太阳前面，清晨升起。

sentences.en: The other followed it, sinking in the evening, as if foreboding dire calamity, for east as well as weSt.
sentences.zh: 另一颗紧随其后，傍晚沉没，仿佛预示着可怕的灾难，东西方皆是如此。

sentences.en: Certainly, one anticipated the day's beginning, and the other the night's, so that they might act as a sign that evils threatened mortals at both times.
sentences.zh: 当然，一颗预示着白天的开始，另一颗预示着夜晚的开始，这样它们就可以作为一个迹象，表明凡人在两个时间都面临着邪恶的威胁。

sentences.en: They bore a fiery torch to the north, as if to start a fire.
sentences.zh: 它们向北方扛着一支火把，仿佛要点燃一场大火。

sentences.en: They appeared in the month of January, and remained for nearly two weeks.
sentences.zh: 它们出现在一月份，持续了将近两周。

sentences.en: At that time, a very serious plague of Saracens plundered the Gauls with miserable slaughter.
sentences.zh: 那时，一场非常严重的萨拉森人瘟疫以悲惨的屠杀掠夺了高卢人。

sentences.en: So that was the Venerable Bede, writing in the Ecclesiastical History of the English People.
sentences.zh: 那是尊者比德在《英格兰教会史》中所写的内容。

sentences.en: Now, Bede, not brilliant at dates, to be fair to him.
sentences.zh: 公平地说，比德对日期的把握并不精妙。

sentences.en: He said this happened in 729.
sentences.zh: 他说这发生在729年。

sentences.en: He's pretty good.
sentences.zh: 他相当不错。

sentences.en: He's the guy who comes up with our dating system.
sentences.zh: 他是那个想出我们约会系统的人。

sentences.en: He's at least three years out here.
sentences.zh: 他在这里至少差了三年。

sentences.en: Probably.
sentences.zh: 很可能。

sentences.en: So he dated the comets to 729, but there wasn't any Saracen invasion of Gorn in 729.
sentences.zh: 所以他把彗星出现的时间定在729年，但729年并没有萨拉森人入侵高卢。

sentences.en: Most scholars think he's got in a muddle, and he's actually talking about 732.
sentences.zh: 大多数学者认为他搞混了，他实际上谈论的是732年。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Which is a bit odd, because he actually claimed that he finished his book a year earlier.
sentences.zh: 这有点奇怪，因为他实际上声称他在一年前就完成了他的书。

sentences.en: So maybe he put this in afterwards.
sentences.zh: 所以他可能是后来把这个加进去的。

sentences.en: I think that's probably the generally held theory.
sentences.zh: 我认为这可能是普遍持有的理论。

sentences.en: And if he did that, then it's witness to the fact that his sense that this is an amazing episode, it's something that's worth recording.
sentences.zh: 如果他这样做了，那就证明了他认为这是一段令人惊叹的插曲，是值得记录的事情。

sentences.en: And also, it bears witness to the fact that the news of this great battle that's been fought, this great Saracen invasion, has kind of crossed the channel.
sentences.zh: 而且，这也证明了这场战斗的消息，这场伟大的萨拉森人入侵，已经穿过了海峡。

sentences.en: It's spread up all the way through England up to Northumbria.
sentences.zh: 它一路传遍英格兰，直达诺森布里亚。

sentences.en: So this is something that really resonates.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一件真正引起共鸣的事情。

sentences.en: And if Bede is writing about this invasion of 732, then this is the earliest witness that we have to it.
sentences.zh: 如果比德写的是关于732年的这次入侵，那么这就是我们拥有的关于它的最早见证。

sentences.en: And it is indeed very dramatic.
sentences.zh: 而且确实非常戏剧性。

sentences.en: It's not surprising that Bede, who's kind of obviously very attuned to the flow of great
sentences.zh: 难怪对伟大事件的流向非常敏锐的比德

sentences.en: events, would have heard of it and been interested in it, because we have two great and formidable generals coming up against one another.
sentences.zh: 会听说并对它感兴趣，因为我们有两个伟大而可怕的将领相互对抗。

sentences.en: So, Abdel Rahman, the Omeyed general, the governor of Spain, I mean, he's already proved himself very, very formidable in battle.
sentences.zh: 所以，阿卜杜勒·拉赫曼，倭马亚将领，西班牙总督，我的意思是，他已经在战斗中证明了自己非常非常强大。

sentences.en: He's overthrown Uthman, he's defeated Odo, he's now heading northwards towards the line of the Loire.
sentences.zh: 他推翻了乌斯曼，击败了厄多，现在正向卢瓦尔河防线进发。

sentences.en: We don't know how large his invasion force is, but it's evidently, you know, I mean, it's large enough to have defeated Uthman, to have swatted aside Odo.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道他的入侵部队有多大，但很明显，我的意思是，它大到足以击败乌斯曼，击退厄多。

sentences.en: And it is also much, much better equipped than the Frankish army.
sentences.zh: 而且它的装备也比法兰克军队好得多、多得多。

sentences.en: I mean, I always remember I had a children's book of history that had an illustration of the Battle of Tor.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我总是记得我有一本儿童历史书，里面有图尔战役的插图。

sentences.en: And the Franks in that were kind of knights on armor.
sentences.zh: 里面的法兰克人有点像穿盔甲的骑士。

sentences.en: And the Arabs all had, you know, they were kind of loosely, you know, wearing their kind of flowing robes.
sentences.zh: 而阿拉伯人都有，你知道的，他们有点宽松地，你知道的，穿着他们那种飘逸的长袍。

sentences.en: A salad in in the ladybirds.
sentences.zh: 瓢虫书里的萨拉丁。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: But actually, it's the other way round.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，情况恰恰相反。

sentences.en: It's the Omeyed forces that are very much heavier in cavalry than the Franks.
sentences.zh: 倭马亚军队的骑兵比法兰克人重得多。

sentences.en: And they're also much, much better equipped.
sentences.zh: 而且他们的装备也好得多、多得多。

sentences.en: So a quote, Bernard S.
sentences.zh: 因此引用伯纳德·S·

sentences.en: Bachrach, whose book on early Carolingian warfare is brilliant on this whole campaign.
sentences.zh: 巴赫拉赫的话，他关于早期加洛林战争的书在这场整个战役中非常精彩。

sentences.en: And he writes that the Arabs had acquired by conquest the arms manufacturing infrastructure of what had been a large part of the eastern half of the Roman Empire.
sentences.zh: 他写道，阿拉伯人通过征服获得了罗马帝国东半部很大一部分地区的武器制造基础设施。

sentences.en: These production resources were far better developed than those found during the early
sentences.zh: 这些生产资源的开发程度远远超过了8世纪初整个帝国在西方的罗马-日耳曼继承国所发现的资源。

sentences.en: 8th century throughout the empire's Romano-German successor states in the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 帝国在西方的罗马-日耳曼继承国。

sentences.en: So basically, you know, their kit is loads, loads better.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，你知道的，他们的装备要好得多、多得多。

sentences.en: And also, the Omeyeds, they're just much richer.
sentences.zh: 而且，倭马亚人只是富得多。

sentences.en: You know, they've had a century and more of plunder behind them.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们背后有一个多世纪的掠夺历史。

sentences.en: They can afford better armor, better helmets, better swords than the Franks have.
sentences.zh: 他们买得起比法兰克人更好的盔甲、更好的头盔、更好的剑。

sentences.en: And on top of that, they're also much more technologically advanced.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，他们在技术上也更加先进。

sentences.en: So there's one key technological development that the Franks can't rival.
sentences.zh: 所以有一个法兰克人无法抗衡的关键技术发展。

sentences.en: And again, to quote Bachrach, finally, the Muslims had the technology to construct the composite recurve bow, which was made from various layers of bone, horn and wood.
sentences.zh: 再次引用巴赫拉赫的话，最后，穆斯林拥有建造复合反曲弓的技术，这种弓由骨头、兽角和木头的各种层压制而成。

sentences.en: These weapons were far superior to the wooden self-bows available to the northerners.
sentences.zh: 这些武器远远优于北方人可用的木质单体弓。

sentences.en: In addition, the shorter and more powerful recurve bow could be used effectively by mounted troops.
sentences.zh: 此外，更短、更有力的反曲弓可以被骑兵有效使用。

sentences.en: And I read that because I don't really know what a recurve bow is.
sentences.zh: 我读这段是因为我真的不知道什么是反曲弓。

sentences.en: I was about to say, it's one where the limbs of the bow kind of curve away.
sentences.zh: 我正要说，它是那种弓的弓臂会向外弯曲的弓。

sentences.en: So it's a sort of more elaborate curve.
sentences.zh: 所以它是一种更复杂的曲线。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So they kind of curl back on themselves, like a horn almoSt.
sentences.zh: 所以它们会向内卷曲，几乎就像一个兽角。

sentences.en: It's the kind you get in the Arabian Nights, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这是你在《一千零一夜》里能看到的那种，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, Arabian Nights kind of bow.
sentences.zh: 对，《一千零一夜》那种弓。

sentences.en: And even because of that, because of the extra sort of tension or whatever, you can have a shorter bow.
sentences.zh: 甚至因为这个，因为额外的张力或其他什么，你可以拥有一把更短的弓。

sentences.en: So in other words, it's easier to fire when you're on horseback.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你在马背上时更容易发射。

sentences.en: And also, apparently, it can go further than the Frankish bows can.
sentences.zh: 而且显然，它比法兰克弓射得更远。

sentences.en: So it's basically a brilliant bow.
sentences.zh: 所以它基本上是一把出色的弓。

sentences.en: It's a great bow.
sentences.zh: 这是一把伟大的弓。

sentences.en: It's a top bow.
sentences.zh: 这是一把顶级的弓。

sentences.en: So basically, you know, this is not a kind of ragtag desert army.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，你知道的，这不是那种乌合之众的沙漠军队。

sentences.en: This is a very, very formidable force and one that effectively is a kind of worthy successor to the Roman armies because it's drawing on those traditions.
sentences.zh: 这是一支非常非常强大的军队，有效地说是罗马军队的一个当之无愧的继承者，因为它借鉴了这些传统。

sentences.en: Now, people who've listened to the first two episodes will remember that the Franks too are drawing on a Roman inheritance.
sentences.zh: 现在，听过前两集的人会记得，法兰克人也借鉴了罗马的遗产。

sentences.en: So they were trained to fight in a Roman way.
sentences.zh: 所以他们接受了罗马式的作战训练。

sentences.en: And that's a tradition that's endured for the two centuries since the fall of the Roman empire in the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 这种传统自西罗马帝国灭亡后的两个世纪以来一直延续至今。

sentences.en: And on top of that, they have Roman military manuals, which we know that they read.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，他们拥有罗马的军事手册，我们知道他们阅读过这些手册。

sentences.en: So like the Romans, they have an emphasis on infantry.
sentences.zh: 所以就像罗马人一样，他们非常重视步兵。

sentences.en: At this point, the Franks do not have the kind of the heavily armored loricati, they're called the kind of the armored horsemen that are the precursors of the Western knight.
sentences.zh: 在这一点上，法兰克人还没有那种被称为重装甲骑兵的loricati，也就是西方骑士的前身。

sentences.en: They are very, very much focused on fighting on foot.
sentences.zh: 他们极度专注于步战。

sentences.en: I think in part, although I gather that this is hugely debated by military historians because they haven't yet adopted the stirrup.
sentences.zh: 我认为部分原因——尽管我听说军事史学家对此争论不休——是因为他们还没有采用马镫。

sentences.en: The stirrup is just kind of being introduced to the land of the Franks at this point.
sentences.zh: 马镫当时正开始传入法兰克人的土地。

sentences.en: So Charles would have had horsemen with him and these were called palatini.
sentences.zh: 因此，查理身边会有骑兵，这些人被称为palatini。

sentences.en: So people who are, you know, his elites who surround him in the palace.
sentences.zh: 也就是那些，你知道的，在宫殿里簇拥着他的精英阶层。

sentences.en: And this is where the word paladins comes from, which is kind of very King Arthur.
sentences.zh: 这就是“圣骑士”（paladins）一词的由来，这很有亚瑟王的风格。

sentences.en: Lancelot and Gawain are the paladins of King Arthur.
sentences.zh: 兰斯洛特和高文就是亚瑟王的圣骑士。

sentences.en: So he does have some of them, but the main focus is on, as I say, on infantry and specifically the Franks fight in a phalanx.
sentences.zh: 所以他确实有一些这样的人，但正如我所说，主要的焦点还是步兵，尤其是法兰克人以方阵作战。

sentences.en: So like the Romans had done, very close order, shields locked together.
sentences.zh: 就像罗马人曾经做过的那样，队形非常紧凑，盾牌紧紧锁在一起。

sentences.en: If they are faced by archers, as the Romans had done, they're able to kind of form a testudo, a tortoise.
sentences.zh: 如果他们面对弓箭手，就像罗马人过去那样，他们能够组成一个特斯图多，也就是龟阵。

sentences.en: So you put the shields up and over your heads and the arrows just kind of bounce off your shields.
sentences.zh: 你把盾牌举到头顶上方，箭矢就会从你的盾牌上弹开。

sentences.en: And they fight so closely together that there's a Frankish report of a battle that was fought
sentences.zh: 他们作战时靠得如此之近，以至于有一份关于一场战役的法兰克报告

sentences.en: a century before the Battle of Tor that describes how the slain had nowhere to fall, but stood in their battle lines, corpse, supporting corpse, as though they were still alive.
sentences.zh: 描述了都尔战役一个世纪前的情景，报告称阵亡者甚至无处倒下，而是站在战斗队列中，尸体支撑着尸体，仿佛他们还活着一样。

sentences.en: So very, very close formation.
sentences.zh: 因此，这是一个非常非常紧密的队形。

sentences.en: So it's a bit like the images of fighting that you get in Bernard Cornwell's books, which are, again, not a massively dissimilar period.
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像伯纳德·康威尔书中出现的战斗场景，而且，这段时期其实相差不大。

sentences.en: People packed in a kind of shield wall, stabbing with their swords relentlessly through the gaps in the enemy line.
sentences.zh: 人们挤成一种盾墙，通过敌方阵线之间的空隙用剑进行不间断的刺杀。

sentences.en: Yeah, the use of the stabbing sword rather than the slashing sword.
sentences.zh: 是的，使用的是刺剑，而不是砍剑。

sentences.en: And I guess people would associate kind of Frankish knights as using a massive, great, heavy slashing sword.
sentences.zh: 我想人们会把法兰克骑士与使用巨大、笨重的重型砍剑联系起来。

sentences.en: But at this point, again, they are using the gladius, as the Romans called it, the kind of the stabbing sword.
sentences.zh: 但在这一点上，他们依然在使用罗马人所说的短剑（gladius），也就是那种刺剑。

sentences.en: So they approximate to a Roman legion more than to anything else.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们比其他任何东西都更接近罗马军团。

sentences.en: And of course, Roman legions were dependent on relentless training.
sentences.zh: 当然，罗马军团依赖于不间断的训练。

sentences.en: And this seems to have been what Charles had given his troops.
sentences.zh: 这似乎正是查理给予其军队的东西。

sentences.en: So, you know, that breathing space that Odo's defeat of the Arabs before the walls of Toulouse had brought Charles.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，厄多在图卢兹城墙前击败阿拉伯人，为查理争取到的那段喘息空间。

sentences.en: He doesn't seem to have wasted it.
sentences.zh: 他似乎并没有浪费它。

sentences.en: He seems to have essentially put his troops through their paces, drilling them and drilling them and drilling them.
sentences.zh: 他似乎基本上让他的军队经历了重重考验，进行了一遍又一遍又一遍的操练。

sentences.en: And even if his men are not as well equipped as the Umayyad forces, they are as well trained.
sentences.zh: 即使他的手下装备不如倭马亚军队，但他们的训练同样精良。

sentences.en: And I think that this is what Charles is relying on to defeat them.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是查理击败他们的依仗。

sentences.en: So those are the armies.
sentences.zh: 这就是双方的军队。

sentences.en: What about the strategy of the two commanders?
sentences.zh: 那两位指挥官的战略如何呢？

sentences.en: So Abdul Rahman's strategy is very plain.
sentences.zh: 因此，阿卜杜勒·拉赫曼的战略非常明确。

sentences.en: He wants to sack the shrine of St. Martin.
sentences.zh: 他想要洗劫圣马丁神殿。

sentences.en: And there are various reasons why he would be particularly keen to do that.
sentences.zh: 他之所以对这一点表现得尤为热衷，有各种各样的原因。

sentences.en: The obvious one is loads of his troops are following him in the expectation of loot.
sentences.zh: 显而易见的一个原因是，他的许多军队跟随他是为了期待战利品。

sentences.en: Most of them, I suspect, are not motivated by a passionate commitment to the teachings of the
sentences.zh: 我怀疑，他们大多数人并不是出于对教义的狂热执着

sentences.en: Quran.
sentences.zh: 古兰经。

sentences.en: They want to get as rich as they possibly can.
sentences.zh: 他们只想尽可能地发财。

sentences.en: And St. Martin's shrine promises them all kinds of goodies.
sentences.zh: 而圣马丁的神殿向他们承诺了各种各样的好东西。

sentences.en: I think Abdul Rahman recognizes the kind of significance to Frankish prestige of the shrine of St. Martin.
sentences.zh: 我认为阿卜杜勒·拉赫曼意识到了圣马丁神殿对法兰克人声望的重要性。

sentences.en: If he can sack it, you know, it'll be a real body blow to the prestige of Shah Martel and his regime.
sentences.zh: 如果他能洗劫它，你知道的，这将对查理·马特及其政权的声望造成沉重打击。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, we've said Abdul Rahman, you know, he comes from the heartlands of Islam.
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道的，我们说过阿卜杜勒·拉赫曼，你知道的，他来自伊斯兰教的核心地带。

sentences.en: He definitely has a kind of a doctrinal motivation.
sentences.zh: 他绝对有一种教义上的动机。

sentences.en: He wants to strip the shrine of St. Martin bear, not just because it's full of treasure, but because as he sees it, it's full of kind of idols.
sentences.zh: 他想剥光圣马丁神殿，不仅因为它满是宝藏，还因为在他看来，里面充满了各种偶像。

sentences.en: He wants to humble the pride of the cross worshipers into the duSt.
sentences.zh: 他要把崇拜十字架者的傲慢践踏成尘埃。

sentences.en: But to do that, to reach the shrine of St. Martin, you know, he's going to have to wipe out the army of the Franks, Charles's army.
sentences.zh: 但要做到这一点，要到达圣马丁神殿，你知道的，他必须消灭法兰克人的军队，也就是查理的军队。

sentences.en: And the reason for that is that Charles's strategy essentially is to block his access to Tor and force him to attempt a decisive battle.
sentences.zh: 原因在于，查理的战略基本上是阻断他通往都尔的通道，并迫使他进行决定性的决战。

sentences.en: And this for Abdul Rahman is going to be a real challenge because even though his men are superior
sentences.zh: 这对阿卜杜勒·拉赫曼来说将是一个真正的挑战，因为尽管他的手下在装备和军事技术上更胜一筹

sentences.en: in kit and in military technology, the Franks, as we've said, are at least as well trained and they're also probably numerically superior.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所说，法兰克人的训练至少同样出色，而且在人数上可能也占优势。

sentences.en: And that's because Charles's forces have been swelled by, you know, the troops that Odo has brought with him from Aquitaine.
sentences.zh: 这是因为查理的军队得到了厄多从阿基坦带来的军队的壮大。

sentences.en: And of course, you know, they are absolutely resolute in their determination to defend
sentences.zh: 当然，你知道的，他们捍卫圣马丁神殿的决心绝对坚如磐石

sentences.en: St. Martin's shrine, just as Abdul Rahman wants to strip it because it's so precious to the Franks.
sentences.zh: 正如阿卜杜勒·拉赫曼想要掠夺它，因为它对法兰克人如此珍贵。

sentences.en: Obviously, for that reason, the Franks are determined to defend and protect it.
sentences.zh: 显然，出于这个原因，法兰克人决心捍卫和保护它。

sentences.en: Charles is confident that this is potentially winning strategy because he can rely on his
sentences.zh: 查理坚信这可能是一个取胜的策略，因为他可以依靠他的手下坚守阵地

sentences.en: men to hold their ground, not to break, not to flee, but also should the Arabs be defeated, not to run after them, you know, which would potentially then open them up to attack
sentences.zh: 不退缩，不逃跑，而且如果阿拉伯人战败，也不要盲目追击——你知道的，这可能会让他们面临阿拉伯骑兵的攻击。

sentences.en: by the Arab cavalry.
sentences.zh: 阿拉伯骑兵。

sentences.en: So this strategy effectively means the late autumn of 732, that a battle is going to be inevitable.
sentences.zh: 因此，这一战略实际上意味着，在732年的晚秋，一场大战将不可避免。

sentences.en: Charles is going to block the road to tour.
sentences.zh: 查理将封锁通往都尔的道路。

sentences.en: Abdul Rahman is going to have to engage him if he wants to break through.
sentences.zh: 阿卜杜勒·拉赫曼如果想突破，就必须与他交战。

sentences.en: And the reason for that, he can't really retreat because that would be very damaging to his prestige.
sentences.zh: 原因在于，他真的不能撤退，因为那会对他的声望造成极大损害。

sentences.en: And also if he retreats, there's a risk to his baggage train with all that kind of gold and stuff.
sentences.zh: 而且如果他撤退，运送那些黄金等物资的辎重队就会面临风险。

sentences.en: So effectively, there is no choice but to engage.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，除了交战别无选择。

sentences.en: So there's essentially a kind of week of shadow boxing.
sentences.zh: 因此，基本上有一周左右的试探期。

sentences.en: And then finally, the moment comes.
sentences.zh: 然后终于，时刻来临了。

sentences.en: The Arabs are on the Roman road.
sentences.zh: 阿拉伯人出现在罗马大道上。

sentences.en: They see the Franks lined up ahead of them.
sentences.zh: 他们看到法兰克人排成阵列在前方等待。

sentences.en: There is no choice now but to engage in battle.
sentences.zh: 现在除了投入战斗别无选择。

sentences.en: And again, the best account of what happens is this chronicle of 754.
sentences.zh: 同样，关于发生的事情最好的记载就是这本754年的编年史。

sentences.en: And the Christian priest writing that, he describes the Frankish battle line in an incredibly memorable way.
sentences.zh: 撰写该书的基督教神职人员以一种令人难忘的方式描述了法兰克人的战线。

sentences.en: The northern has held their position like a glacier from the frozen north.
sentences.zh: 北方人坚守阵地，宛如来自北方冰原的冰川。

sentences.en: I mean, amazing description.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个惊人的描述。

sentences.en: Kind of impassable, immovable, indomitable.
sentences.zh: 某种不可逾越、不可动摇、不可战胜的存在。

sentences.en: But also icy cold and dangerous.
sentences.zh: 但同时也冰冷而危险。

sentences.en: He describes how the stabbing swords of the Franks, the gladi, inflict terrible damage on the invaders.
sentences.zh: 他描述了法兰克人的短剑（gladi）如何给侵略者造成了可怕的杀伤。

sentences.en: And among the dead is Abdul Rahman himself.
sentences.zh: 死者当中就包括阿卜杜勒·拉赫曼本人。

sentences.en: So again, the Chronicle of 754.
sentences.zh: 所以再次提到754年的编年史。

sentences.en: The Austrasians, so that's the Franks, with a terrible strength in their limbs and an iron hand throughout the hard fight, killed him when they found him.
sentences.zh: 奥斯特拉西亚人，也就是法兰克人，四肢有着可怕的力量，在艰苦的战斗中以铁血手腕，在找到他时将他杀死。

sentences.en: Then comes, it's clear that the victory is the Franks.
sentences.zh: 随后到来的是，很明显胜利属于法兰克人。

sentences.en: But what is perhaps the most impressive witness to their discipline is that they hold their line.
sentences.zh: 但对他们的纪律而言，或许最令人印象深刻的证明是他们坚守了防线。

sentences.en: I mean, as I said, it's the only way that they could have lost at this point would be if they kind of go, whoa, we've won.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，正如我所说，他们在这个时候唯一可能会输的情况，就是他们那种“哇，我们赢了”的心态。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: And piled off.
sentences.zh: 然后一哄而散。

sentences.en: They don't.
sentences.zh: 他们没有这样做。

sentences.en: They hold their positions and then they retreat to their camp pretty confident that the next day they're going to have to fight again, that the battle will continue.
sentences.zh: 他们坚守阵地，然后退回营地，深信第二天还得继续战斗，战斗将继续下去。

sentences.en: And I'll describe what then happens and what they find when they wake up the day after this first engagement by quoting the Chronicle of 754.
sentences.zh: 我将通过引用754年的编年史来描述接下来发生的事情，以及他们在经历第一次交战后的第二天醒来时发现了什么。

sentences.en: So this priest writes, rising from their sleeping bags at dawn, the Europeans, and it's such an interesting use of that.
sentences.zh: 所以这位神父写道，欧洲人在黎明时分从睡袋中醒来——这个词的用法太有趣了。

sentences.en: I mean, I think it's the first use of that phrase in any medieval chronicle.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为这是任何中世纪编年史中首次使用这个短语。

sentences.en: The Europeans beheld the tents and camps of the Arabs canopies located and ordered as they had been, not knowing that they were all empty and supposing that the Saracens phalanxes
sentences.zh: 欧洲人看到阿拉伯人的帐篷和营地依然像以前一样安放和排列着，并不知道它们都已经空了，还以为萨拉森人的方阵

sentences.en: were prepared for battle within.
sentences.zh: 已经在里面准备好战斗了。

sentences.en: They sent scouts and found that all the Ishmaelites' columns had escaped.
sentences.zh: 他们派出侦察兵，发现所有的伊斯迈尔人纵队都已经逃跑了。

sentences.en: So that's the Arab columns.
sentences.zh: 也就是阿拉伯人的纵队。

sentences.en: And that all of them were secretly fleeing home, passing the night in tight formation.
sentences.zh: 他们全都秘密连夜逃回了家，一路保持着紧密的队形。

sentences.en: The Europeans were anxious lest they might have concealed themselves on a hidden path as a stratagem.
sentences.zh: 欧洲人担心他们可能会作为某种战术而隐藏在某条隐蔽的小路上。

sentences.en: Stunned in every way, they hunted the surrounding area in vain.
sentences.zh: 他们感到震惊万分，徒劳地搜寻了周边地区。

sentences.en: Making no further effort to find the aforesaid people, they returned to their own countries rejoicing with their booty and the evenly divided spoils.
sentences.zh: 在没有做出进一步努力去寻找上述人员后，他们带着战利品和平分得到的 spoils 欢欣鼓舞地返回各自的国家。

sentences.en: So that's it.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这样。

sentences.en: The invaders, the raiders, have been beaten off and they've vanished with their stuff because they don't want to lose their, what plunder they've already gained.
sentences.zh: 侵略者、突袭者被击退了，他们带着自己的东西消失了，因为他们不想失去已经获得的战利品。

sentences.en: I think they leave some of it behind and this is what the Franks pick up.
sentences.zh: 我想他们留下了一部分，这就是法兰克人拾到的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But the Franks don't pursue them.
sentences.zh: 但法兰克人并没有追击他们。

sentences.en: I mean, that's what's striking.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这才是最令人震惊的地方。

sentences.en: They let them go.
sentences.zh: 他们放过了他们。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it's indisputably, for them, a great victory.
sentences.zh: 对他们来说，这无疑是一场伟大的胜利。

sentences.en: St. Martin is safe.
sentences.zh: 圣马丁安全了。

sentences.en: St. Martin is safe and his shrine will never be threatened again.
sentences.zh: 圣马丁安全了，他的神殿再也不会受到威胁了。

sentences.en: But this leads open to the question that we began this episode with.
sentences.zh: 但这引发了我们在本集开始时提出的问题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: What is the significance of this battle?
sentences.zh: 这场战役究竟有什么重大意义？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, is it world historical in its moment?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，它在当时具有世界历史意义吗？

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And I guess the first question is, what do we make of this attack that the Améad forces have launched on the Loire?
sentences.zh: 我想第一个问题是，我们如何看待倭马亚军队对卢瓦尔河发动的这次进攻？

sentences.en: Is it a raid?
sentences.zh: 这只是一次突袭吗？

sentences.en: Is it a maneuver in a kind of factional battle between assorted Christian and Muslim warlords?
sentences.zh: 这是各路基督教和穆斯林军阀派系斗争中的一次机动吗？

sentences.en: Is it a Muslim attempt to humble a Christian shrine?
sentences.zh: 这是穆斯林试图羞辱基督教神殿的行为吗？

sentences.en: I reckon the answer to that is that it's all of those.
sentences.zh: 我认为答案是，这些因素都有。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: I mean, they're not mutually exclusive.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它们并不是相互排斥的。

sentences.en: You know, the desire for loot, the ambition that Abdel Rahman had to punish the treachery of Uthman and to kind of humble Odo into the dust, his zeal for Islam.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，对战利品的渴望，阿卜杜勒·拉赫曼惩罚奥斯曼背叛并羞辱厄多的野心，他对伊斯兰教的热忱。

sentences.en: I mean, all of these are clearly part of the mix of motivations, I think, that are encouraging him.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，所有这些显然都是激励他的动机的一部分。

sentences.en: But what it isn't is a long-planned, cold-blooded, coordinated, massive invasion.
sentences.zh: 但它绝不是一次蓄谋已久、冷酷无情、协调一致的大规模入侵。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: It's not that.
sentences.zh: 它不是那样的。

sentences.en: It isn't.
sentences.zh: 确实不是。

sentences.en: But I think that doesn't mean that it's not significant.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着它不重要。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Let's do a counterfactual.
sentences.zh: 让我们做一个反事实假设。

sentences.en: Abdel Rahman wins.
sentences.zh: 阿卜杜勒·拉赫曼赢了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Charles Martel is killed.
sentences.zh: 查理·马特被杀。

sentences.en: Odo is killed.
sentences.zh: 厄多被杀。

sentences.en: They march on the Shrine of St. Martin.
sentences.zh: 他们向圣马丁神殿进军。

sentences.en: They strip it bare.
sentences.zh: 他们洗劫一空。

sentences.en: And then they cart all the treasure back.
sentences.zh: 然后把所有的宝藏都运了回去。

sentences.en: And what happens next?
sentences.zh: 接下来会发生什么？

sentences.en: You know, we can never be sure in any of these situations.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在任何这种情况下我们都无法百分之百确定。

sentences.en: So, you know, there are so many kind of intangibles.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，有太多不确定因素了。

sentences.en: But the balance of probability would be that Aquitaine would definitely fall to the Améad forces.
sentences.zh: 但概率上讲，阿基坦肯定会落入倭马亚军队手中。

sentences.en: I mean, if Odo is dead, if his men have been wiped out, there's no real prospect of the Améad forces not occupying it and kind of making it a forward base beyond the Pyrenees.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果厄多死了，如果他的手下被消灭了，倭马亚军队不占领它并将其变成比利牛斯山以北的前进基地，这种可能性微乎其微。

sentences.en: The one thing I would say is if they have that, they have to keep supplying it with men and
sentences.zh: 我要说的一点是，如果他们占领了那里，他们就必须不断从比利牛斯山以南运送人员

sentences.en: whatnot from beyond the Pyrenees, which does look like a pretty significant natural barrier through most of history between France and Spain.
sentences.zh: 等等，而在历史上大部分时间里，比利牛斯山看起来确实是法国和西班牙之间一道意义重大的天然屏障。

sentences.en: They do.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: But then the Straits of Gibraltar are also a pretty significant barrier.
sentences.zh: 但直布罗陀海峡同样也是一道相当重要的屏障。

sentences.en: And they've managed to take Spain.
sentences.zh: 而他们还是成功攻占了西班牙。

sentences.en: And I think part of the reason for that is that success attracts followers.
sentences.zh: 我认为部分原因在于，成功会吸引追随者。

sentences.en: And there would undoubtedly have been people in Aquitaine who would have wanted to side with the winners.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，阿基坦会有人想要站在胜利者一边。

sentences.en: And that would then have provided a kind of reserve of manpower.
sentences.zh: 而这本来会提供某种人力储备。

sentences.en: That the Améad occupiers could have drawn on.
sentences.zh: 供阿米亚德占取者调用。

sentences.en: And if they do that, then the consequences of that for southern Gaul are pretty clear.
sentences.zh: 如果他们这么做了，那么这对南高卢造成的后果将是显而易见的。

sentences.en: I mean, southern Gaul will become part of the Améad caliphate.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，南高卢将成为阿米亚德哈里发国的一部分。

sentences.en: And that in turn, I think, would have put Italy in peril.
sentences.zh: 而我认为，这反过来又会把意大利置于危险之中。

sentences.en: And Italy, of course, is the home of the papacy in Rome.
sentences.zh: 当然，意大利是罗马教皇的发源地。

sentences.en: And the Byzantine forces there are, you know, under attack.
sentences.zh: 那里的拜占庭军队正在遭到攻击。

sentences.en: You've made a massive leap in the course of a sentence from they'd probably got Aquitaine to suddenly Italy has fallen as well.
sentences.zh: 你在短短一句话里跨度极大，从他们可能占领了阿基坦突然跳到意大利也沦陷了。

sentences.en: Like your dominoes are falling very quickly.
sentences.zh: 就像你的多米诺骨牌倒得非常快。

sentences.en: Well, if southern Gaul falls, then the Franks can't come to the rescue of the papacy.
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果南高卢沦陷，那么法兰克人就无法营救教皇了。

sentences.en: And as we will see in our next episode, essentially in this century, the papacy is dependent for its political survival on Frankish support.
sentences.zh: 正如我们将在下一集中看到的，基本上在本世纪，教皇的政治生存要依赖法兰克人的支持。

sentences.en: So I think it's improbable that the papacy that Rome would have held out against Muslim domination had Tor gone the other way.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，如果图尔战役走向相反，罗马教皇绝不可能抵挡住穆斯林的统治。

sentences.en: And the implications of that would have been pretty significant.
sentences.zh: 而这带来的影响将是相当深远的。

sentences.en: I mean, what about the implications for the independent Frankish kingdom?
sentences.zh: 我是说，这对独立的法兰克王国意味着什么？

sentences.en: I mean, it's got huge reserves of manpower.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它拥有巨大的人力储备。

sentences.en: It could easily have rallied.
sentences.zh: 它本可以轻易地重新集结。

sentences.en: It could have held out.
sentences.zh: 它本可以坚守下去。

sentences.en: It could have launched a reconquest of the south.
sentences.zh: 它本可以发动对南方的收复失地之战。

sentences.en: That, after all, is what, you know, in the long run, the Spanish Christians do over the course of the Middle Ages.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，从长远来看，这正是西班牙基督徒在中世纪过程中所做的事情。

sentences.en: But I think that there are two episodes from early medieval history that suggest that it would have been a challenge.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，中世纪早期的两个历史插曲表明，这将会是一个巨大的挑战。

sentences.en: It would have been difficult for the Franks to do that.
sentences.zh: 法兰克人要做到这一点将会非常困难。

sentences.en: And the first, of course, is what we've just been talking about, the defeat of the Visigoths.
sentences.zh: 当然，第一件事就是我们刚才一直在谈论的，西哥特人的战败。

sentences.en: Because if you say, you know, the attack on Tor was just a raid.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你说，对图尔的进攻只是一次突袭。

sentences.en: Well, essentially, the invasion across the Straits of Gibraltar into Spain was just a raid.
sentences.zh: 那么，从本质上讲，穿过直布罗陀海峡入侵西班牙也只是一次突袭。

sentences.en: But because the invaders won this massive battle and killed the Visigothic king, within a decade, pretty much the whole of Spain had fallen into their lap.
sentences.zh: 但由于入侵者赢得了这场重大战役并杀死了西哥特国王，在十年之内，几乎整个西班牙都落入了他们的囊中。

sentences.en: And, you know, with Aquitaine as a base, I think the potential for a kind of campaigns of jihad against the Franks in the north would have been considerable, which isn't to say
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，以阿基坦为基地，我认为对北方法兰克人发动圣战的潜在可能性将是相当巨大的，这并不是说

sentences.en: that the same thing would have happened, but it might have done.
sentences.zh: 同样的事情一定会发生，但它确实有可能发生。

sentences.en: We don't know.
sentences.zh: 我们无从得知。

sentences.en: But the other event that I think, you know, had the Shrine of St. Martin been sacked, there is then an obvious parallel later in the century.
sentences.zh: 但我认为还有另一件事，如果圣马丁神庙被洗劫，那么本世纪晚期就会有一个明显的相似之处。

sentences.en: Which you alluded to right at the beginning of this episode.
sentences.zh: 你在本集一开始就暗示过这一点。

sentences.en: And that's what the Vikings do when they launch their campaigns against particularly England.
sentences.zh: 那就是维京人对特别是英格兰发动战役时的做法。

sentences.en: And that begins with the sack of a famous shrine, the Shrine of St. Cuthbert on Holy Island, the island of Lindisfarne.
sentences.zh: 这始于对一个著名神圣之地的洗劫，即圣岛林迪斯法恩岛上的圣卡斯伯特神庙。

sentences.en: And what that demonstrates is that to loot a shrine that has a kind of a special holiness is never just to loot it.
sentences.zh: 这表明，洗劫一个具有特殊神圣性的神庙，绝不仅仅是掠夺财务。

sentences.en: Because as well as the financial loss, there is also the shock that it delivers to people for whom this shrine is a kind of central part of their spiritual identity.
sentences.zh: 因为除了经济损失之外，它还给那些将这座神庙视作其精神认同核心部分的人们带来了巨大的冲击。

sentences.en: So the sack of the Shrine of St. Cuthbert on Lindisfarne sends shockwaves, not just across
sentences.zh: 因此，对林迪斯法恩圣卡斯伯特神庙的洗劫，其产生的冲击波不仅波及了

sentences.en: Britain, but across the whole of Europe.
sentences.zh: 英国，而是整个欧洲。

sentences.en: And I think it, you know, it gives a pretty devastating blow to Northumbrian morale.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，它对诺森布里亚人的士气造成了毁灭性的打击。

sentences.en: And the Kingdom of Northumbria falls to pieces fairly soon afterwards.
sentences.zh: 不久之后，诺森布里亚王国便四分五裂了。

sentences.en: And I think that the sack of the Shrine of St. Martin would have had probably an even greater impact.
sentences.zh: 我认为，洗劫圣马丁神庙可能会产生更大的影响。

sentences.en: St. Martin is the great patron of Frankish royalty.
sentences.zh: 圣马丁是法兰克王室伟大的守护神。

sentences.en: But by the 8th century, it's become much more than that.
sentences.zh: 但到了八世纪，它已经远不止于此了。

sentences.en: So St. Martin, you know, he's the first, he's the most celebrated of all Gauls, monks, of all Gauls, holy men.
sentences.zh: 所以圣马丁，他是所有高卢修士、所有高卢圣人中最著名的一个。

sentences.en: And he has become the emblem of a kind of common identity that has joined Franks and Romans.
sentences.zh: 他已经成为了将法兰克人和罗马人联系在一起的共同身份认同的象征。

sentences.en: They all share a kind of common devotion to this saint.
sentences.zh: 他们都对这位圣人怀有一种共同的崇敬之情。

sentences.en: And so you could say that the sack of St. Martin's Shrine would have been a blow, not just
sentences.zh: 所以你可以说，圣马丁神庙的洗劫不仅是对法兰克威望的打击，

sentences.en: to Frankish prestige, but to the very spiritual identity of, you know, this emergent Frankish nation.
sentences.zh: 也是对这个新兴的法兰克民族的精神认同本身的打击。

sentences.en: And of course, at the same time, it would have offered evidence for those with eyes to see of the truth of the message that is being proclaimed by the invaders.
sentences.zh: 当然，与此同时，它也将为那些有眼光的人提供证据，证明入侵者所宣扬的信息是真实的。

sentences.en: And it's absolutely true that this is not kind of at the forefront of the Amayyad campaign.
sentences.zh: 完全正确，这并非阿迈亚德战役的核心前沿。

sentences.en: It's not particularly what they are proclaiming.
sentences.zh: 这并不是他们刻意宣扬的内容。

sentences.en: And therefore, very few people at the point where the Battle of Taur is being fought really have a sense of anything approximating to Islam.
sentences.zh: 因此，在图尔战役爆发之时，极少有人真正对伊斯兰教有一个近似的概念。

sentences.en: So this is why it's not couched by contemporary chroniclers as, you know, a great clash of civilizations or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么当时的编年史家没有把它描述为一场伟大的文明冲突或类似的事情。

sentences.en: So Bede, who we've referenced this, you know, the great scholar and historian writing in his monastery up in Northumbria, he has only the vaguest sense of who the Saracens, as he
sentences.zh: 因此，我们提到过的伟大学者和历史学家比德，他在诺森布里亚的修道院里写作，他对被他称为萨拉森人的人，

sentences.en: calls them, you know, vaguest sense of who they are.
sentences.zh: 只有最模糊的概念，根本不知道他们是谁。

sentences.en: He thinks that they're pagans, that they're worshipers of the morning star.
sentences.zh: 他认为他们是异教徒，是晨星的崇拜者。

sentences.en: There are others who are closer to them who think of them essentially as Christian heretics.
sentences.zh: 还有一些离他们更近的人，本质上把他们视为基督教异端。

sentences.en: Which is so common.
sentences.zh: 这是非常普遍的。

sentences.en: That's what Christians think of them in the early years of Islam, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 在伊斯兰教的早期，基督徒就是这么看他们的，对吧？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I think right the way through to the Middle Ages, I mean, Dante is still kind of, you know, that's still how he's framing them.
sentences.zh: 我认为一直到中世纪，但丁仍然在用这种方式来看待他们。

sentences.en: I mean, they don't really have a sense of Islam as a religion.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们并没有真正将伊斯兰教视为一种宗教。

sentences.en: I mean, that's a much later kind of conceptualization.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那是一种晚得多的概念化理解。

sentences.en: And maybe because of that, maybe because Islam in some ways is very close to Christianity, you
sentences.zh: 也许正因如此，也许是因为伊斯兰教在某些方面与基督教非常接近，

sentences.en: know, Jesus is in the Quran, Virgin Mary's in Quran, both Christianity and Islam have a respect for the Hebrew prophets.
sentences.zh: 耶稣在《古兰经》中，圣母玛利亚在《古兰经》中，基督教和伊斯兰教都对希伯来先知表示尊敬。

sentences.en: That is a big difference, I think, between the Muslim invaders of Spain and Gaul and the
sentences.zh: 我认为，西班牙和高卢的穆斯林入侵者与维京人之间有着一个巨大的区别，

sentences.en: Vikings, because there are doubtless people in England who do end up abandoning their Christianity and turning to the worship of the Viking gods.
sentences.zh: 因为英格兰确实毫无疑问地有人最终放弃了基督教，转而崇拜维京神明。

sentences.en: But it's not a sophisticated framework of belief.
sentences.zh: 但这不是一个成熟的信仰框架。

sentences.en: And the kind of structures of imperialism that the Vikings bring are, you know, it's basically kind of grab it and settle.
sentences.zh: 维京人带来的那种帝国主义结构，基本上就是抢夺和定居。

sentences.en: And that's the limit of it.
sentences.zh: 这就是它的极限。

sentences.en: But the evidence of Muslim Spain shows that Islam is very, very different, that it has a very sophisticated relationship to Christianity.
sentences.zh: 但穆斯林西班牙的证据表明，伊斯兰教非常非常不同，它与基督教有着非常复杂的关系。

sentences.en: It has a framework for subordinating Christians and Jews and kind of, you know, putting them within an empire.
sentences.zh: 它拥有一套征服基督徒和犹太人并将他们纳入帝国之中的框架。

sentences.en: The Quran mandates how they should be taxed, how they should be subordinated, all these kind of things.
sentences.zh: 《古兰经》规定了应该如何对他们征税，如何使他们臣服，以及所有诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: It's a program for imperial rule.
sentences.zh: 这是一个帝国统治的纲领。

sentences.en: And that is an obvious point of differentiation between the Vikings and the Arabs.
sentences.zh: 这是维京人和阿拉伯人之间明显的区别所在。

sentences.en: And that's why Spain, it's not just that it is ruled by Muslims, it becomes Muslim over the course of the centuries that follow its conqueSt.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么西班牙不仅由穆斯林统治，而且在其征服后的几个世纪里彻底变成了穆斯林国家。

sentences.en: And I think you could suppose the Muslims hold on to southern Gaul.
sentences.zh: 我想你可以假设穆斯林坚守了南高卢。

sentences.en: You could see the same process happening there.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到同样的过程在那里发生。

sentences.en: You know, that would have pretty seismic implications for the future course of medieval history.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那将对中世纪历史的未来走向产生震撼性的影响。

sentences.en: And I think ultimately, to think that the annihilation of Charles Martel's army has no real significance, that it's just a raid, that it's, you know, nothing very important.
sentences.zh: 我认为归根结底，认为查理·马特的军队被全歼没有任何实际意义，认为这只是一次突袭，认为这并不重要，

sentences.en: And I think ultimately, to suppose that had Charles Martel lost the battle, had he died, had his troops been wiped out, had the Shrine of St. Martin been attacked, that it was just
sentences.zh: 我认为归根结底，假设查理·马特输掉了战役，假设他死了，假设他的部队被全歼，假设圣马丁神庙遭到袭击，这仅仅只是一次突袭，

sentences.en: a raid.
sentences.zh: 这只是一次突袭。

sentences.en: I think that to kind of believe that, it's effectively to argue that Islam and Christianity, and
sentences.zh: 我认为持有这种看法，实际上等同于在争辩说伊斯兰教与基督教，

sentences.en: specifically the distinctive form of Christianity that emerges in Western Europe in the centuries after the Battle of Taur, that they're essentially the same.
sentences.zh: 特别是图尔战役之后几个世纪在西欧兴起的独特形式的基督教，它们本质上是一样的。

sentences.en: There's no real difference between them.
sentences.zh: 它们之间没有真正的区别。

sentences.en: It doesn't really matter if you're ruled by Christians or by MusliMs.
sentences.zh: 你是被基督徒统治还是被穆斯林统治其实并不重要。

sentences.en: And I just don't think that's true.
sentences.zh: 我只是认为事实并非如此。

sentences.en: I think that there is a very, very profound difference between the two ways of seeing the world.
sentences.zh: 我认为这两种看待世界的方式之间存在着非常非常深层的差异。

sentences.en: And so therefore, I think that the Battle of Taur is significant.
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为图尔战役意义重大。

sentences.en: I mean, I don't think it's a kind of peripheral clash.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我不认为这是一场边缘化的冲突。

sentences.en: I think it is momentous, perhaps not quite as momentous as Gibbon suggested, but pretty important.
sentences.zh: 我认为它是重大的，也许不像吉本所暗示的那样具有划时代意义，但相当重要。

sentences.en: And Charles Martel's victory, in that sense, is pretty seismic in the long run.
sentences.zh: 从长远来看，查理·马特的胜利在某种意义上是具有震撼性的。

sentences.en: But it's seismic also in the short term, because it has very important implications for the future of the Frankish kingdom and for his own dynasty.
sentences.zh: 但它在短期内同样具有震撼性，因为它对法兰克王国的未来以及他自己的王朝有着极其重要的影响。

sentences.en: Are there not some other reasons why you could question the idea about the momentousness of this battle?
sentences.zh: 难道没有其他一些理由可以让你质疑这场战役具有划时代意义的观点吗？

sentences.en: So, for example, the Maillard Chronicles often mention big defeats.
sentences.zh: 所以，例如，马亚德编年史经常提到惨重的失败。

sentences.en: So they mention defeats in the early stages of the Reconquista, for example.
sentences.zh: 比如，它们提到了收复失地运动早期的失败。

sentences.en: But they never mention this at all.
sentences.zh: 但它们根本没有提及这件事。

sentences.en: Like, it doesn't even feature.
sentences.zh: 就像它甚至没有出现过一样。

sentences.en: They treat it as a raid that just, you know, just one raid among many and beaten back.
sentences.zh: 他们把它当成了一次突袭，你知道的，仅仅是众多突袭中的一次，而且被击退了。

sentences.en: I looked this up.
sentences.zh: 我查过资料。

sentences.en: There were more raids in 734.
sentences.zh: 在734年还有更多突袭。

sentences.en: There was a raid in 736.
sentences.zh: 736年也有一次突袭。

sentences.en: And there was actually, some people think, an even bigger raid, even bigger invasion in
sentences.zh: 事实上，有些人认为在

sentences.en: 739 when the Umayyads got to Burgundy, only to be beaten back by the Franks.
sentences.zh: 739年发生了一次更大规模的突袭、更大规模的入侵，当时倭马亚人到达了勃艮第，结果却被法兰克人击退了。

sentences.en: So in other words, this was not the end of their incursions.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这并不是他们入侵的终点。

sentences.en: So in that sense, it's not really a turning point.
sentences.zh: 从这个意义上说，这并不算是一个真正的转折点。

sentences.en: It doesn't change anything because they just keep coming.
sentences.zh: 它没有改变任何事情，因为他们一直在卷土重来。

sentences.en: I think it is, for reasons that we'll look at in the next episode, because it means it's not just the Franks have won.
sentences.zh: 我认为它是，出于我们将在下一集中探讨的原因，因为它意味着不仅仅是法兰克人赢了。

sentences.en: Charles Martel has won.
sentences.zh: 查理·马特赢了。

sentences.en: The kind of the glory of his victory kind of resonates to his prestige.
sentences.zh: 他胜利的荣耀提升了他的威望。

sentences.en: And as we will see, he is now in a position not just to defend his kingdom against the invaders, but to go on the offensive.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所见，他现在不仅有能力保卫自己的王国免受入侵者的侵害，而且还能转入进攻。

sentences.en: And his son, in turn, will be able to do that.
sentences.zh: 他的儿子也将能够做到这一点。

sentences.en: And his grandson, who is Charlemagne, will definitely be able to do that.
sentences.zh: 他的孙子，也就是查理曼大帝，绝对能够做到这一点。

sentences.en: But there's one other thing which is even more important, which I think is arguably much more important than the Battle of Tor.
sentences.zh: 但还有一件事更重要，我认为它可以说比图尔战役要重要得多。

sentences.en: And that's in 740, a huge revolt breaks out in what's now Morocco, Great Berber Revolt.
sentences.zh: 那就是在740年，现在的摩洛哥爆发了一场巨大的起义，即伟大的柏柏尔起义。

sentences.en: And that basically cuts off Umayyad, Spain, from the sort of Arab heartland.
sentences.zh: 这基本上切断了倭马亚西班牙与阿拉伯腹地的联系。

sentences.en: It means that the age of raiding kind of comes to an end, because they can't keep raising all the, you know, there's so much internal dissension.
sentences.zh: 这意味着掠夺的时代走向了终结，因为他们无法不断集结，你知道的，内部有如此多的纷争。

sentences.en: And the Umayyads can't keep raising all these Berber troops.
sentences.zh: 而且倭马亚人无法继续征召所有这些柏柏尔军队。

sentences.en: So that would seem to undermine the idea that, oh, they get Aquitaine, then they get this,
sentences.zh: 所以这似乎削弱了这样一种观点：哦，他们得到了阿基坦，然后得到了这个，

sentences.en: then they get this, then they get this, because actually they've got so many problems in their
sentences.zh: 然后得到了这个，接着又得到了那个，因为实际上他们在自己的后院里遇到了如此多的问题，

sentences.en: own kind of backyard, as it were, that they were actually never going to be able to do all that because of the massive ructions going on in North Africa.
sentences.zh: 以至于由于北非发生的巨大动乱，他们实际上永远不可能完成所有这些事。

sentences.en: No, I don't think so.
sentences.zh: 不，我不这么认为。

sentences.en: Because what also then happens after that is that, and we've did this in our history of
sentences.zh: 因为在那之后发生的事情是，我们在巴格达的历史中讲过，

sentences.en: Baghdad, is that the Umayyads are overthrown by the Abbasids.
sentences.zh: 倭马亚王朝被阿拔斯王朝推翻了。

sentences.en: But one of the Umayyads is able to get to Spain, where he establishes himself as its ruler, and in the long term as its caliph.
sentences.zh: 但其中一位倭马亚王族成员成功逃到了西班牙，在那里他建立了统治，并从长远来看成为了哈里发。

sentences.en: And this is the great golden age of Umayyad Spain.
sentences.zh: 这就是倭马亚西班牙伟大的黄金时代。

sentences.en: And it's ferociously and impressively formidable.
sentences.zh: 它极其凶猛且令人印象深刻。

sentences.en: It's a very potent military power, and it's a very great kind of civilizational power.
sentences.zh: 它是一种非常强大的军事力量，也是一种非常伟大的文明力量。

sentences.en: And this is the period when you see large numbers of Christian Spaniards converting to
sentences.zh: 正是在这段时期，你会看到大量的西班牙基督徒皈依

sentences.en: Islam, because it has this kind of great force of appeal.
sentences.zh: 伊斯兰教，因为它具有这种巨大的吸引力。

sentences.en: It's culturally, militarily, politically more appealing than Christianity, which seems a
sentences.zh: 它在文化、军事、政治上比基督教更有吸引力，基督教似乎是一种被打败的、被取代的看待世界、

sentences.en: kind of defeated and superseded way of seeing the world, way of explaining man's relationship to God.
sentences.zh: 解释人类与上帝关系的方式。

sentences.en: And had that realm that the Umayyads take over in the wake of the Abbasid Revolution, had that extended to southern Gaul, had it extended to northern Italy, then, you know,
sentences.zh: 如果倭马亚革命后倭马亚人接管的那个王权扩展到了南高卢，扩展到了意大利北部，那么，

sentences.en: that would have been an even larger power base for the Umayyad caliphate.
sentences.zh: 那将为倭马亚哈里发国提供一个更加庞大的权力基础。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Well, if people want to listen to that, they've got an episode on Umayyad Spain, which I greatly recommend.
sentences.zh: 如果人们想听这个，他们有一集关于倭马亚西班牙的节目，我强烈推荐。

sentences.en: But for the time being, we're going to be going on with the story of the Franks, right,
sentences.zh: 但目前，我们将继续讲述法兰克人的故事，对吧，

sentences.en: Tom?
sentences.zh: 汤姆？

sentences.en: So what's coming up next?
sentences.zh: 那么接下来要讲什么？

sentences.en: So coming up next, it's the son of Shah Martel and his relationship with the papacy,
sentences.zh: 接下来要讲的是查理·马特的儿子以及他与教皇的关系，

sentences.en: which is, again, a development of seismic impact for the future history of Europe, and therefore, in the long run, the world.
sentences.zh: 这同样对欧洲未来历史、并因此从长远来看对世界的未来具有震撼性影响的发展。

sentences.en: And this man, Pippin, who overthrows the Merovingians, makes himself king.
sentences.zh: 这个人就是矮子丕平，他推翻了墨洛温王朝，自立为王。

sentences.en: He is the father of a much greater and more famous king, Charlemagne.
sentences.zh: 他是更伟大、更著名的国王查理曼大帝的父亲。

sentences.en: And so at the end of our next episode, Charlemagne will be entering the story.
sentences.zh: 因此，在我们的下一集结束时，查理曼大帝将登场。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: So next up is our Charlemagne trilogy, one of the most epic stories we've ever done on
sentences.zh: 所以接下来是我们的查理曼三部曲，这是我们在《历史就是这样》节目中做过的最具史诗感的故事之一。

sentences.en: The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 《历史就是这样》。

sentences.en: Now, the good news, if you're a member of The Rest is History Club, is that you should have all three parts of that trilogy right now.
sentences.zh: 好消息是，如果你是《历史就是这样》俱乐部的会员，你现在就应该能收听到这个三部曲的所有三个部分。

sentences.en: Now, if you're not a member of the club and you'd like to get your hands on them, all you need to do is head to therestishistory.com and sign up, and you can have that Charlemagne
sentences.zh: 如果你不是俱乐部会员，又想听这些内容，你所需要做的就是前往therestishistory.com并注册，你就可以立即收听查理曼

sentences.en: trilogy straight away.
sentences.zh: 三部曲了。

sentences.en: If not, I'm afraid you'll just have to wait.
sentences.zh: 如果不是的话，恐怕你就只能等着了。

sentences.en: See you then.
sentences.zh: 到时见。

sentences.zh: 拜拜。
